note: The build spec is the preregistration document: every analysis it names was specified before any data existed. Anything added during the build is exploratory, including additions that were forced by an asset turning out to be missing. Listed honestly in both directions, per G5's requirement.
prereg_document: Claude Code Build Spec: Introspection Factorization

specified.what: P(report) = f1 x f2 x f3, with f1 a cross-validated mass-mean probe at 5% FPR on control trials, f2 the concept token inside top-k of the J-lens readout at the report position, f3 the judge scoring the generation as naming the concept
|f1*f2*f3 - observed| reported as a raw number at every k and in both orders
counts entering f1 and surviving each stage
f1 recomputed with shuffled labels
matched-norm random vectors through the identical pipeline; f2 thresholds as a quantile of this rather than an absolute value
f2 at the report, injection and a random position
f2 over k in {1,5,10,25,50} with the null band overlaid
f2 at each of the three readout layers
leave-one-concept-out range on each factor
f3 recomputed with judge disagreements flipped, as an interval
same pipeline under the R-lens if available
TPR and FPR with Wilson intervals per (layer, strength), TPR-FPR as the discriminability scalar, AUC across the strength ladder
the Godet confound: same vectors injected into unrelated yes/no questions whose default answer is no
Hartigan dip test on the per-concept detection distribution with a p-value
Spearman between our per-concept rates and Macar's Gemma rates, with CI
specified.status: NOT COMPUTED -- the per-concept Gemma rates are not published anywhere reachable; see ASSETS.md section 12

specified.what: top-10 most frequent wrong identifications with counts
abstract/concrete split before and after the single-token filter
Cohen's kappa against 50 hand-labelled responses plus the confusion matrix
specified.status: PENDING -- requires human labels; G3 emits the sample and computes kappa once they exist

specified.what: alpha=0 versus no hook at all, max absolute logit difference
B=4 batched versus 4 singles, reported as a raw number
max absolute residual difference outside the injection window at the injection layer and every layer below
target token probability versus alpha, Spearman per concept
confusion matrix on a 10-concept subset
perplexity of generated text versus clean, per alpha
J-lens, logit lens and a random-rotation null lens compared on rank, not only hit rate
reading the target at randomly chosen positions
KS against uniform for prompt-irrelevant tokens
J-lens and logit lens agreement rising toward the last fitted layer
intermediate entity surfacing earlier in depth than the final answer
fraction of top-10 readouts that are special tokens, byte fragments or non-words
a control statistic compared between the first and last decile of shards
cross-condition claims restated at a common FPR
number of comparisons across the condition grid and BH-adjusted q-values for headline claims
minimum detectable effect at 80% power for any null being claimed
confidence interval on the difference between orders

exploratory.what: concepts stratified on detection measured by this project over the full single-token pool, rather than on Macar's Gemma rates
exploratory.why: the specified rates are not published; see ASSETS.md section 12. Avoids cross-model regression to the mean, but forfeits the cross-model Spearman.

exploratory.what: the bimodality dip is computed on the whole single-token pool, not on the selected 60
exploratory.why: the 60 were selected to span the detection range, which would manufacture the spread. The selected-60 dip is also reported, explicitly labelled selection-induced.

exploratory.what: the assistant turn is prefilled up to the detection key so the next token is a JSON boolean in both orders
exploratory.why: the report position is only well defined for report-first otherwise; reading both orders at the last prompt token would compare a detection verdict against a task answer and call the difference an order effect.

exploratory.what: control_zero cells are computed once per (batch, order) and broadcast across strengths and across both vector arms
exploratory.why: alpha=0 adds exactly zero whatever the vector is, which G2 measures, so this is exact rather than an approximation. Kept per-batch so the drift probe still has a per-batch statistic.

exploratory.what: the injection is Garcia's workspace_band: one intervention at every layer 24-40, each scaled by the LIVE median residual norm read inside that layer's hook
exploratory.why: specified as a single layer at Garcia's per-layer strength, which is ~17x weaker in cumulative displacement (23x measured on a toy stack) and produced 1e-4 dose-response and 0.000 detection in every cell. The policy change is a correction of a misconfiguration, not a new analysis, but it invalidates every number measured under the old one -- so all of G2, G3 and the first sweep are superseded rather than compared against.

exploratory.what: the grid carries two injected objects at matched norm: per-layer concept vectors (arm A, headline) and per-layer J-lens rows (arm B, Garcia's own object)
exploratory.why: arm B is a positive control -- if it does not reproduce his steering and report rates the harness is at fault rather than the model. A-vs-B at equal ||delta|| is also a causal manipulation of J-space loading, which is the verbalizability factor; that reading was NOT prespecified and is exploratory.

exploratory.what: concept vectors are extracted at every band layer rather than extracted once and reused across the band
exploratory.why: injecting a layer-27 vector at layer 38 is a cross-layer mismatch; under a 17-layer band 16 of the 17 injections would be that mismatch. Costs nothing, since the layers come off one forward.

exploratory.what: concept i takes TASK_PROMPTS[i % 10] in all of its cells, in the pilot and in the sweep
exploratory.why: with one fixed task every control_zero cell was the same forward pass, so FPR rested on as many trials as there were task prompts and the whole result was hostage to one prompt. The task is held fixed WITHIN a concept so its injected and control cells stay paired.

exploratory.what: the 60 concepts are re-piloted and re-stratified under the band at the chosen operating point
exploratory.why: the existing 60 were tier-selected on floor noise -- every pilot rate sat at the detection floor of a ~20x-too-weak injection, so the selection was effectively random. The reselect is EXPLORATORY: it is a second pass at a selection step whose first pass is known to be uninformative, and tiers remain a sampling device that is never a reporting unit.

exploratory.what: f1 reads the residual at layer 40, the band's last layer, rather than at the injection layer
exploratory.why: under a band there is no single injection layer; 40 is the deepest point the intervention is still being written to, and the report position's own depth.

exploratory.what: the position control draws its comparison position from ALL non-injected, non-report positions
exploratory.why: it previously drew only from [0, first_injected), which is the system-prompt prefix -- the same tokens every trial, and causally upstream of the injection, so it could not have carried the concept even in principle. The wider draw includes the positions after the span, where leakage would actually appear.

exploratory.what: the report-position rank is computed both from the sweep cache and from a fresh forward, and the agreement reported
exploratory.why: catches the sweep and the factor pass having built different prompts.

exploratory.what: the end-to-end report rate is reported both cascade-consistently and naively, with the gap
exploratory.why: the gap is trials that name the concept without clearing the probe or the readout -- leakage in the operationalisation rather than a property of the model.

exploratory.what: the composition audit uses three buckets (concrete / abstract / mixed) rather than a forced binary
exploratory.why: professions, science terms, sports, music/art, weather and actions-as-nouns are neither cleanly; forcing them would invent a split.

exploratory.what: every interval on a factor is a bootstrap over concepts, not over trials
exploratory.why: f1 and f2 are shared across the samples drawn from one prefill residual, so trials are not independent.

exploratory.what: a second independent J-lens fit as a robustness arm
exploratory.why: camilablank/workspace-lenses hosts a different fit of the same object; bounds how much of f2 is lens-fit noise.

exploratory.what: G1 reports both the published item-level fraction and a word-level proportion
exploratory.why: the published metric is a mean of per-item fractions, which is not a raw proportion, so Wilson does not apply to it.

exploratory.what: identification scored by word-boundary match accepting singular forms, with the LLM judge optional and explicitly flagged when unavailable
exploratory.why: the concept list is plural; a model naming 'trumpet' for 'Trumpets' is a correct identification. Keeps the pipeline runnable without an API key, but 'the judge said so' and 'a regex said so' are different claims and are never conflated.
